definitions.explanation: A lamp or light fixture installed along streets and roads to illuminate public areas at night.

examples.japanese: {街灯|がいとう}が{暗|くら}い{道|みち}を{照|て}らしている。
examples.english: The streetlights illuminate the dark road.

examples.japanese: この{通|とお}りは{街灯|がいとう}が{少|すく}なくて、{夜|よる}は{怖|こわ}い。
examples.english: This street has few streetlights, so it's scary at night.

examples.japanese: {古|ふる}い{街灯|がいとう}がLEDに{交換|こうかん}されて、{街|まち}が{明|あか}るくなった。
examples.english: The old streetlights were replaced with LEDs, making the town brighter.

notes:
A compound of {街|がい} (street, town) and {灯|とう} (light, lamp).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {街灯|がいとう}が{灯|とも}る (streetlights come on)
- {街灯|がいとう}の{下|した} (under a streetlight)
- {街灯|がいとう}の{光|ひかり} (streetlight glow)
- {街灯|がいとう}が{少|すく}ない (few streetlights)

Synonymous with {街路灯|がいろとう}, though {街灯|がいとう} is more concise and common in everyday usage. In literature and song lyrics, {街灯|がいとう} often evokes a moody, atmospheric nighttime scene.

COUNTER: {本|ほん} or {基|き}
